newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee ends lower.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee ends lower.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee closed lower against the dollar as dollar holders held on to the U.S unit as it gained overseas, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 58.43 to the dollar after opening at 58.33, they said.

"The dollar held its own despite a lack of demand because of a lack of selling. Speculators expect the Central Bank to revalue the currency on Tuesday due to overseas gains," said a Standard Chartered Bank dealer.

The Central Bank, which sets the dollar-rupee exchange rate daily after considering local demand and supply, overseas movement and cross currency fluctuations, revalued the U.S. unit by 10.25 local cents on Monday.
Buying and selling prices were fixed at 57.6279 and 58.7921 since the collar had gained significantly overseas, dealers said.
Overnight call money rates closed at 19 percent after opening at 14, they said.
The volatility in call rates is due to heavy cash calls ahead of next week's Sinhala and Tamil New Year, dealers said.
A lot of money goes out of banks at this time by way of bonuses and festival advances, and returns to the system in about a month.
